source_records.inspection: full NIST accepted manuscript, published PDF via web, and numerical supplements inspected
findings: Updated constants and empirical levels form PW2024; partition and caloric evaluations are tabulated over 1-5000 K.
Section 3.3 uses conservative expanded upper/lower-bound uncertainty estimates with coverage factor two and includes unbound-state uncertainty.
The 2025 uncertainty prescription does not by itself uniquely establish the cause of every central-table/direct-sum difference.
Supplemental H and U(H) column values are J/mol despite kJ/mol labels; closure against partition moments verifies the correction.
Supplemental S already removes the nuclear-spin product; it must not be divided by four again.
All supplied levels contribute to direct moments; first-dissociation cutoff is a separate sensitivity diagnostic, not a total-atomization energy replacement.

model_boundary.interpretation: Positive excess is consistent with additional thermodynamic contributions and the 2016 unbound-treatment lineage; unique numerical attribution is not established. The Cp difference exceeds the published Cp uncertainty; few above-threshold discrete levels do not explain it.

decision: No production change in this investigation. Prioritize a thermodynamically consistent 2025 thermal candidate at the current total ATcT energy anchor, then test a conserved finite substitution.
